subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: a golden-yellow house key made of brass. Will it stick to a magnet?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: peetal ki bani sunehri ghar ki chaabi. Kya woh magnet se chipkegi?
answer: No; brass (made of copper and zinc) is not magnetic.

subject: science
prompt_en: A paper clip is at the bottom of a glass of water. Predict: can you drag it up the side of the glass without touching the water, by moving a strong magnet outside the glass?
prompt_hi: Paani ke glass ke andar neeche ek paper clip padi hai. Guess karo: kya bahar se tez magnet ghuma kar, paani ko chhoo-e bina, clip ko glass ki deewar ke saath upar la sakte ho?
answer: Yes; magnetic force acts through glass and water, so the clip follows the magnet.

subject: science
prompt_en: You correctly said aluminium foil won't stick. Why not, if it is a metal?
prompt_hi: Tumne sahi kaha ki aluminium foil nahi chipkegi. Agar woh dhaatu hai toh kyon nahi?
answer: Only some metals are magnetic (iron, nickel, cobalt and alloys like steel that contain them); aluminium is a non-magnetic metal.

subject: science
prompt_en: An iron safety pin and an aluminium hair clip both look silvery and shiny. How can you tell them apart without scratching or tasting them?
prompt_hi: Lohe ki safety pin aur aluminium ka hair clip dono chandi jaise chamakte hain. Bina khurche ya chakhe dono ko kaise alag pehchaanoge?
answer: Test with a magnet: the iron pin is attracted, the aluminium clip is not.

subject: science
prompt_en: A kabadiwala has a heap of mixed steel food tins and aluminium drink cans. How could he quickly separate them?
prompt_hi: Ek kabadiwale ke paas steel ke dabbe aur aluminium ke cold drink ke cans ka mila hua dher hai. Woh jaldi se inhe kaise alag karega?
answer: Use a strong magnet: the steel tins are pulled out and the aluminium cans are left behind.

subject: science
prompt_en: Sand from a river bank sometimes has tiny black grains that stick to a magnet wrapped in a plastic bag. What might those grains contain?
prompt_hi: Nadi kinare ki ret mein kabhi-kabhi chhote kaale daane hote hain jo plastic bag mein lipte magnet se chipak jaate hain. Un daanon mein kya ho sakta hai?
answer: Iron (an iron-containing mineral), since only magnetic materials like iron are attracted.

subject: science
prompt_en: Make a two-column chart, 'Attracted' and 'Not attracted', and place: iron nail, plastic scale, steel paper clip, copper wire, rubber eraser, nickel strip.
prompt_hi: Do column ka chart banao, 'Kheencha gaya' aur 'Nahi kheencha gaya', aur rakho: lohe ki keel, plastic scale, steel paper clip, taambe ka taar, rubber, nickel ki patti.
answer: Attracted: iron nail, steel paper clip, nickel strip. Not attracted: plastic scale, copper wire, rubber eraser.

subject: science
prompt_en: Golu wrote: 'All metals stick to magnets; that's how we know if something is a metal.' Find his mistake.
prompt_hi: Golu ne likha: 'Saari dhaatuein magnet se chipakti hain; isi se pata chalta hai ki koi cheez dhaatu hai.' Uski galti dhundho.
answer: Many metals (aluminium, copper, brass, gold, silver) do not stick; a magnet test shows whether something is magnetic, not whether it is a metal.

subject: science
prompt_en: Explain to your younger cousin which things a magnet can pick up, and why 'shiny metal' isn't enough to know.
prompt_hi: Apne chhote cousin ko samjhao ki magnet kaunsi cheezein utha sakta hai, aur 'chamakdaar dhaatu' hona kaafi kyon nahi hai.
answer: Key ideas: magnets attract iron, nickel, cobalt and many steels; they don't attract aluminium, copper, brass, plastic or wood; shiny doesn't mean magnetic, so test it; even some steel spoons don't stick.

subject: science
prompt_en: From last time: name one metal that is NOT attracted by a magnet.
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: ek aisi dhaatu batao jise magnet nahi kheenchta.
answer: Any one: aluminium, copper, brass, gold, silver.

subject: science
prompt_en: What happens when you bring the north pole of one magnet near the south pole of another? And north near north?
prompt_hi: Ek magnet ka north pole doosre ke south pole ke paas laao toh kya hota hai? Aur north ke paas north?
answer: North and south attract each other; north and north repel each other.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: in the school lab, your teacher places a sheet of paper over a bar magnet and sprinkles iron filings on it. Where will the filings gather the most?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: school lab mein teacher bar magnet ke upar ek kaagaz rakh ke uspe lohe ka buraada chhidakti hain. Buraada sabse zyada kahan jama hoga?
answer: At the two ends (the poles), with far fewer in the middle.

subject: science
prompt_en: Imagine (just in your head, never try it, since real magnets break into sharp pieces): a bar magnet breaks into two halves. If you bring the broken ends back towards each other, the same way they were joined, will they attract or repel? Predict.
prompt_hi: Sirf dimaag mein socho (asli magnet kabhi mat todna, uske tukde nukeele hote hain): ek bar magnet do tukdon mein toot jaata hai. Toote hue siron ko waise hi wapas paas laao jaise jude the, toh woh kheenchenge ya dhakelenge? Guess karo.
answer: They attract, because new opposite poles form at the break; each half is a complete magnet.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: two ring magnets are slid onto a pencil held upright, with like poles facing each other. What will the top magnet do?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: do ring magnet ek khadi pencil mein daale gaye, ek jaise poles aamne-saamne. Upar wala magnet kya karega?
answer: It floats (hovers) above the lower magnet, because like poles repel.

subject: science
prompt_en: You saw the top ring magnet float. Why doesn't it fall down onto the lower one?
prompt_hi: Tumne dekha upar wala ring magnet tair raha tha. Woh neeche wale pe gir kyon nahi jaata?
answer: Like poles face each other and repel; the upward push balances the magnet's weight.

subject: science
prompt_en: An iron nail and a bar magnet are both pulled by your magnet. What test can show which one is the magnet?
prompt_hi: Lohe ki keel aur ek bar magnet, dono tumhare magnet se kheenche jaate hain. Kaunsa test batayega ki inme magnet kaunsa hai?
answer: The repulsion test: bring each end near one pole of your magnet; if an end is pushed away, that object is a magnet. The iron nail is only ever attracted.

subject: science
prompt_en: You have a tiny magnet from a toy kit and a large black fridge magnet. How would you find out which is stronger?
prompt_hi: Tumhare paas toy kit ka ek chhota magnet aur fridge ka ek bada kaala magnet hai. Kaise pata karoge kaun zyada taakatwar hai?
answer: Compare what each can do with the same paper clips: count how many each lifts, or how far away each can pull a clip; don't judge by size.

subject: science
prompt_en: In a magnetic toy train, each carriage joins the next using magnets at its ends. One carriage refuses to join and pushes away. What is happening, and how can you fix it?
prompt_hi: Magnetic toy train mein har dibba agle se magnet ke zariye judta hai. Ek dibba judne ki jagah door dhakelta hai. Kya ho raha hai, aur kaise theek karoge?
answer: Like poles are facing each other and repelling; turn the carriage around so unlike poles face each other and attract.

subject: science
prompt_en: Draw two bar magnets for each case and add arrows showing push or pull: (a) N facing S, (b) S facing S.
prompt_hi: Har case ke liye do bar magnet banao aur teer se dikhao kheenchna ya dhakelna: (a) N ke saamne S, (b) S ke saamne S.
answer: (a) Arrows pointing towards each other: attraction. (b) Arrows pointing away from each other: repulsion.

subject: science
prompt_en: Golu says: 'If I cut my magnet in half, I'll get a north-only magnet and a south-only magnet.' What is wrong?
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Agar main magnet ko beech se kaat doon, toh ek sirf-north aur ek sirf-south magnet milega.' Galti kya hai?
answer: Each piece has both a north and a south pole; magnetic poles always come in pairs.

subject: science
prompt_en: Teach your friend the 'rules' of magnets: poles, attraction and repulsion, and how to look after magnets.
prompt_hi: Apne dost ko magnet ke 'niyam' sikhao: poles, kheenchna aur dhakelna, aur magnet ki dekhbhaal kaise karein.
answer: Key ideas: every magnet has N and S poles, strongest at the ends; like poles repel, unlike attract; repulsion is the sure test; breaking a magnet makes new poles; strength isn't size; heating, hammering or dropping weakens magnets, so store them in pairs with keepers.

subject: science
prompt_en: From last time: what is the sure test to know that an object is a magnet?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: kisi cheez ke magnet hone ka pakka test kya hai?
answer: Repulsion: if it pushes away a pole of a known magnet, it is a magnet.

subject: science
prompt_en: Your compass needle has settled. How do you find east?
prompt_hi: Tumhare compass ki suyi ruk gayi hai. East (poorab) kaise pata karoge?
answer: Turn the compass so the N on the dial lines up with the needle's north end; east is then marked E, a quarter turn clockwise from north (to your right if you face north).

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: you hang a bar magnet from a thread, gently turn it to point east-west, and let go. What will happen?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: bar magnet ko dhaage se latka ke halke se east-west mein ghumaao aur chhod do. Kya hoga?
answer: It swings and settles back into the north-south direction.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: you stroke a straightened steel paper clip about 30 times in one direction with one pole of a magnet, then float it on a piece of cork in a bowl of water. What will the clip do?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: seedhi ki hui steel ki paper clip ko magnet ke ek pole se ek hi disha mein 30 baar ragdo, phir use cork ke tukde pe rakh ke paani ki katori mein tairao. Clip kya karegi?
answer: It turns and settles pointing north-south like a compass, because stroking made it a magnet.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: you slowly bring a bar magnet close to a compass lying on the table. What happens to the needle?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: mez pe rakhe compass ke paas dheere-dheere bar magnet laao. Suyi ka kya hoga?
answer: The needle swings away from north and turns towards the magnet (its north end is pulled by the magnet's south pole and pushed by its north pole); magnets disturb a compass.

subject: science
prompt_en: You said the floating paper clip points north-south. Why does it do that?
prompt_hi: Tumne kaha tairti hui paper clip uttar-dakshin mein rukti hai. Woh aisa kyon karti hai?
answer: Stroking turned it into a magnet, and since the Earth behaves like a giant magnet, the clip magnet lines up north-south.

subject: science
prompt_en: Compare a compass placed on a wooden table and one placed on top of a steel almirah. Which reading can you trust, and why?
prompt_hi: Lakdi ki mez pe rakha compass aur steel ki almari ke upar rakha compass compare karo. Kis reading pe bharosa kar sakte ho, aur kyon?
answer: The one on the wooden table; the iron or steel in the almirah can pull on the needle and give a wrong reading.

subject: science
prompt_en: Your group must find which wall of a new classroom faces east, using a compass. What steps will you follow?
prompt_hi: Tumhare group ko compass se pata karna hai ki nayi class ki kaunsi deewar east ki taraf hai. Kaun se steps loge?
answer: Hold the compass flat, away from iron and magnets; let the needle settle; turn the compass so N lines up with the needle's north end; look in the direction marked E; the wall in that direction faces east.

subject: science
prompt_en: Long ago, sailors far out at sea, with clouds hiding the Sun and the stars, still found their direction. How?
prompt_hi: Bahut pehle naavik samundar ke beech mein, jab baadal Suraj aur taaron ko chhupa dete the, tab bhi disha dhundh lete the. Kaise?
answer: They used a magnetic compass (a magnetised needle or lodestone), which points north-south in any weather.

subject: science
prompt_en: Draw a compass face and mark N, E, S and W. If you face north, which direction is on your right?
prompt_hi: Compass ka chehra banao aur N, E, S, W likho. Agar tum north ki taraf mooh karo, toh tumhare right haath pe kaunsi disha hogi?
answer: East is on your right, west on your left and south behind you.

subject: science
prompt_en: Golu says: 'A compass needle points north because it is so cold at the North Pole, and magnets like cold.' What is wrong?
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Compass ki suyi north isliye dikhati hai kyonki North Pole pe bahut thand hai, aur magnet ko thand pasand hai.' Galti kya hai?
answer: Cold has nothing to do with it; the Earth behaves like a giant magnet, and the needle lines up with it.

subject: science
prompt_en: Explain to a younger child how to make a pin-and-water compass (with an adult holding the pin) and why it works.
prompt_hi: Ek chhote bachche ko samjhao ki pin aur paani wala compass kaise banate hain (pin kisi bade se pakadwa ke) aur woh kaam kyon karta hai.
answer: Key ideas: stroke a steel pin or straightened paper clip many times in one direction with one pole of a magnet (an adult helps with anything sharp); float it on cork or a leaf in water; it turns north-south because it became a magnet and lines up with the Earth's magnetism; keep it away from other magnets and iron.

subject: science
prompt_en: From last time: the end of a freely hanging magnet that points north is called its ___ pole.
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: khule latke magnet ka jo sira north ki taraf hota hai, use ___ pole kehte hain.
answer: North (north-seeking) pole.

subject: science
prompt_en: How many centimetres are in 1 metre, and how many millimetres are in 1 centimetre?
prompt_hi: 1 metre mein kitne centimetre hote hain, aur 1 centimetre mein kitne millimetre?
answer: 100 cm in 1 m; 10 mm in 1 cm.

subject: science
prompt_en: One end of a pencil is at 0 cm and the other end at 14.5 cm. How long is the pencil?
prompt_hi: Pencil ka ek sira 0 cm pe hai aur doosra 14.5 cm pe. Pencil kitni lambi hai?

subject: science
prompt_en: Your scale's end is broken, so the first clear mark is 1 cm. An eraser lined up from 1 cm ends at 5.5 cm. Predict what Golu, who only reads the end mark, will say, and what the real length is.
prompt_hi: Tumhari scale ka sira toota hai, pehla saaf nishaan 1 cm hai. 1 cm se rakha rubber 5.5 cm pe khatam hota hai. Guess karo, jo Golu sirf aakhri nishaan padhta hai, woh kya bolega, aur asli lambai kya hai?
answer: Golu will say 5.5 cm; the real length is 5.5 − 1 = 4.5 cm.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: Riya reads the same mark on a scale once from the left, once from directly above and once from the right. Will all three readings be the same?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: Riya scale ka ek hi nishaan ek baar left se, ek baar seedha upar se aur ek baar right se padhti hai. Kya teeno reading same aayengi?
answer: No; readings taken from the sides will be off, and only the reading from directly above is correct.

subject: science
prompt_en: Why can't a tailor note your kurta measurements in her handspans?
prompt_hi: Darzi aapke kurte ka naap apni baalisht mein kyon nahi likh sakti?
answer: Handspans differ between people, so anyone else cutting the cloth would get different sizes; a standard unit like cm on a measuring tape gives the same value for everyone.

subject: science
prompt_en: Two ways of measuring a book: (A) the scale laid along the book's edge starting at 0; (B) the scale held at a slant, starting from its outer edge. Which is correct, and what is wrong with the other?
prompt_hi: Kitaab naapne ke do tareeke: (A) scale kitaab ke kinare ke saath, 0 se shuru; (B) scale tircha, uske bahari kinare se shuru. Kaunsa sahi hai, aur doosre mein kya galat hai?
answer: A is correct. B is slanted, not along the length, and starts from the edge instead of the zero mark, so it gives a wrong reading.
